text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- SPD accuses governemnt of deception and bungling. Finance Minister Theo Waigel concedes in emergency budget debate that Federal Labour Office will get government subsidy next year.
- Pension funds will be short of around seven billion marks in 1997 if the government does not raise premiums, they say.
- Hilmar Kopper to leave post as Deutsche Bank chairman in 1997.
- Former finance minister Gerhard Stoltenberg says proposed tax reforms could net around 20 billion marks in 1999.
HANDELSBLATT
- Rolf Breuer replaces Hilmar Kopper at head of Deutsche Bank.
- Kopper's resignation seen as skilful manoeuvre.
- Insurers demand higher premiums.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel concedes Bonn will pay subsidy to Federal Labour Office in 1997.
- Brussels wants to give Deutsche Telecom green light to grant discounts to major customers.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- The hole in the budget is getting bigger. Next year the Federal Labour Office to receive a government subsidy.
- Hilmar Kopper to resign early from Deutsche Bank, Rolf-Ernst Breuer to become chairman.
- Judge dismisses VW defamation lawsuit against rival Adam Opel AG.
- Pension funds want premiums raised to 20.2 percent.
DIE WELT
- Call for change in fiscal policy. Government rejects opposition SPD charge in emergency debate that this year's budget is unconstitutional and passed borrowing limits at the end of September.
- Deutsche Bank chairman Hilmar Kopper to leave Europe's biggest bank and be replaced by Rolf-Ernst Breuer.

- Schroeder shuffles Lower Saxony cabinet, appointing chief of staff Willi Waike as finance minister after Hinrich Swieter resigned. Swieter is suspected of sexual harassing a woman in his constituency.
- Prosecutor in Stuttgart trial of Daimler Benz management says in confidential letter that investigation against Juergen Schrempp and Hilmar Kopper will be dropped.
- VW libel case against Opel dismissed in Frankfurt court.
- German towns and villages in a fix -- they're threatened with a flood of sewage from housing developments.
